description: DEFECT 1 (data loss): the IaC/plan analyzer catches that the plan REPLACES the RDS instance — the database is destroyed and recreated

DEFECT 2 (oversize): the plan sizes the database at db.r6g.4xlarge — the FinOps-relevant field the security scan never looks at
DEFECT 2: priced against the good baseline, the oversize database blows past the 2x threshold — FinOps blocks
DEFECT 3 (exposure): the security scan catches the 0.0.0.0/0 rule opening Postgres (5432) to the internet — the defect neither the IaC nor the FinOps stage would flag
DEFECT 3: the sensitive exposure blocks the plan on security review
THE POINT: run the full specialist chain over the one cheap-prompt plan and it BLOCKS — no single stage catches all three, the chain does
COVERAGE: the chain surfaces FOUR independent blockers (IaC replace, security exposure, cost, rollback) from the single plan — each stage earned its place
ROLLBACK: because the plan destroys the datastore, the change reviewer judges it irreversible — approval requires a restore-from-backup plan
WHY A CHAIN: the security scan alone, run on the STATEFUL-REPLACE-only plan, sees nothing wrong — a single reviewer misses defects outside its lane
